author: dapplion
content: Without recursive proofs I find eip8025 useless. What's its purpose then?

author: dapplion
content: My take is that EIP8025 can allow a fraction of stakers to run without EL at the Gloas fork, reducing cost and giving relief to low powered home stakers for example. But we need the mechanism to be sound.

author: dapplion
content:
Re-reading the EIP motivation:
- Constant-time payload verification: only applies if you have no EL
- Stateless verification: only applies if you have no EL

To have no EL we need recursive proofs

author: jsign
content:
<@688748669268132001> here are the arguments for proposing 8025 https://github.com/eth-act/eip-8025/blob/main/ACD.md
The main one is having green-light to upstream changes in to execution-specs, since already all the changes (without recursive proofs) are ~[16k lines of code](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/2268) (I edited the pr description recently) -- not really touching STF, but new prover artifacts lead to new fields in eest fixtures; so it is mostly a lot of internal testing infra changes.

We haven been working on this for quite a lot of time with more than 15 official EEST releases plus two benchmark releases. We feel this is mature enough to plant a flag and propose upstreaming the changes.

If we don't do this, it will be hard to keep rebasing such a big branch for more than a year (at a minimum), plus trying to create further branches to understand how zkEVM interact with other upcoming changes (like PBT) which will live in other branches. (So we would have to rebase a separate branch on top of another separate branch). 

For now we feel is safer to propose these 16k lines as they are today, and we can definitely keep iterating on recursive proofs in execution-specs (and benchmarks and understand implications) afterwards more towards mandatory proofs.

Maybe from the CL angle 8025 looks simpler from the spec side; but from the EL-specs isn't really a trivial change, so we want to derisk already settling all the work that we know is solid and properly tested and refined.

author: jsign
content: The work on zkEVM project isn't done with 8025 alone. We still need to go further with recursive proving which not only has EL-spec changes but also zkVM design implications, know how that affects performance improvements, potential repricings of opcodes, wait for PBT code chunking, etc. So I wouldn't say we should need the endgame be 8025; that's the main reason is named "Optional" since even with recursive proofs, you can't still call it done. That's a separate goal we call "Mandatory proofs" in a future fork.

author: jsign
content:
> To have no EL we need recursive proofs
And to be clear: 8025 EIP text explicitly clarifies no CL is allowed to attest using proofs; so 8025 does not allow not having an EL since isn't safe yet.
